quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When following a car, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors. This position helps you stay visible.

questions.question: Is hearing protection recommended when riding?

options.text: Not recommended if you have a full-face helmet.
Not recommended when riding with passengers.
Not a concern for those with good hearing.

questions.explanation: Even with a helmet, wind and engine noise can damage your hearing. Earplugs protect your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like car horns and sirens.

questions.question: Where should cargo be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep cargo low and secure it or place it in saddlebags. Piling cargo high on the back can raise the center of gravity and throw off the motorcycle's balance. Always balance cargo equally on both sides.

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.
questions.explanation: Alcohol causes many motorcycle crashes, especially fatal ones. Nearly 40 percent of riders killed in motorcycle accidents had been drinking.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.

questions.explanation: In risky areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hand ready on the clutch and both brakes. This lets you react faster to hazards.

questions.question: Why shouldn't riders rely only on mirrors to see what's around them?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller than car mirrors, so you can't see as much.
Motorcycles, like cars, have blind spots.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles, like cars, have blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Turn your head to check your blind spots regularly.

questions.question: Oil collects in the center of the lane. When should this area be avoided?

options.text: Should be avoided if it is raining.
Offers the best traction in the lane.
Will allow you to ride faster than other parts of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided if it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of each lane. In dry conditions, this area has enough traction for safe riding. In rain, avoid it because oil makes it slippery.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right, why shouldn't you ride in the right portion of your lane?

options.text: Drivers may get out of a vehicle unexpectedly.
Car doors may open into your lane.
Pedestrians may step out from between cars.
Other motorists may think you're trying to park.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other motorists may think you're trying to park.
questions.explanation: Stay in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from doors opening, drivers getting out, and people stepping out from between cars.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another rider on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Get into the right part of the lane so you can be seen in their side mirror.
Get into the left part of the lane to increase your line of sight.
Stay in the center part of the lane so you can be seen in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to draw attention to yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get into the left part of the lane to increase your line of sight.
questions.explanation: Move to the left portion of your lane to see better and be more visible to drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes have equal power.
The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
You should only use the front brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about 70 percent of your stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: On a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel tired.
Wear warm clothes to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
Ride more than 12 hours in a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothes to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take breaks every two hours. Do not use stimulants—they cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do everything except:

options.text: Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, making your motorcycle slower to respond. Ride slower, slow down earlier, and stay farther behind other vehicles. Always tell your passenger about hazards ahead.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders when looking through turns.
Keep your knees away from the fuel tank.
Turn only your head and eyes when looking through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes when looking through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through turns to where you want to go. Turn your head only, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best or always bad. Change your position based on the road and traffic around you.

questions.question: An oily strip forms in the center of lanes from vehicle drippings. You should:

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when the road is wet.
Ride only on the oily strip because it gives better grip.
Stay away from the entire center part of the lane.
Not worry about oil or debris in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil builds up in the center of lanes from dripping vehicles. When the road is dry, the strip usually has enough grip for motorcycles. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride to either side and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action first, then the other.
Do both at the same time with extra braking pressure.
Do both at the same time, focusing mainly on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good grip to swerve safely, so do not brake and swerve at the same time. Do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: Since other drivers have trouble seeing motorcycles at night, riders should:

options.text: Ride directly in front of other vehicles so headlights show you.

questions.explanation: Ride slower at night and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of cars ahead to see farther. Use your high beam (unless following or meeting other vehicles). Be flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: During the day, your headlight should be:

options.text: Switched between high and low beam.

questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day to help other drivers see you. Use high beam anytime you are not riding behind or toward other vehicles.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you, why should you not move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The side closest to the passing vehicle is better.
You will feel more wind blast on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay on the side of your lane closest to the passing vehicle. Moving to the far side may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: What formation should a group of riders use when entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Use a single-file formation when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway. A staggered formation is best for riding on straight roads while staying close together.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together whenever you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should a rider do when entering a turn?

options.text: Move their shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, reduce your speed by releasing the throttle and applying both brakes if needed.

questions.question: How do motorcycle headlights compare to car headlights?

options.text: They are usually just as powerful.

questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: What helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, use both brakes, and avoid sudden movements. Stay away from the center of the lane and follow the tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: Under ideal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Maintain at least a two-second following distance under normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What is true about the center portion of a lane?

options.text: It is always the best part of the lane for motorcycles.
It often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
It often has oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
It is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of each lane. Unless the road is wet, this area usually has enough traction for motorcycles. Avoid large buildup of oil and grease, especially at busy intersections and toll booths.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, why should you ride on the left side of your lane?

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
It gives you a better view of hazards in the next lane.
People don't expect to be passed on their left.
It puts you in the rearview mirror of the car in front.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a better view of hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass on the left. This position improves your view of the road ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If hit by a wind blast from a passing vehicle, where should you be riding to have the most room to correct?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane
In the center portion of the lane
In the right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most space to recover if a wind blast affects your control.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, what is the best group formation?
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is good for regular riding. But when going through curves, turns, or entering or leaving a highway, riders should use single-file formation.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket while riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Riding jackets help prevent dehydration and protect you from injury, even in warm weather. Many jackets are designed to keep riders from overheating.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain?
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are bad.

questions.question: What formation should a group of riders use when going through a curve?
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is normally good. But in curves, turns, or when entering or leaving a highway, riders should switch to single-file formation.

questions.question: If you carry a load in a sidecar, how does it affect your motorcycle's stopping distance?

options.text: Will be similar to a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Extra weight in a sidecar makes your motorcycle heavier. This increases how hard it is to stop. Start braking earlier when carrying a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. You are more likely to notice how the motorcycle handles differently.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) makes a person age 21 or older legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: A person of legal drinking age with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. It is safest to assume that any vehicle that could hit you will.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: You are able to see the roadway through vehicles in front of you.
There is pleasant and clear weather.

questions.explanation: Two seconds is normally enough distance. Increase it when you need more stopping time, such as in heavy traffic, bad weather, at night, or when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should:

options.text: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Wear hearing protection only on long rides.
Not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Not use hearing protection if wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs protect your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: The center of a traffic lane is where:

options.text: Debris and oil from cars often collect.
Motorcycle riders should always travel for safety.
Drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil from cars often collect.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane collects debris and oil drippings from cars. Utility hole covers and other hazards are also found there.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT cause a motorcycle to wobble?
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to get out of a wobble.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's total braking power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Check your mirrors carefully in all of these situations, except:

options.text: After you get off the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you get off the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when stopped at an intersection, before changing lanes, and before slowing down. Regular mirror checks are important.

questions.question: In a group ride, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: In the front of the group.
Close to the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This prevents them from having to chase the group. It also allows experienced riders behind them to watch and help.

questions.question: When exiting a highway in a group, which formation should you use?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for group riding. Switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then re-apply it.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep it locked until the motorcycle stops.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until the motorcycle stops.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until you come to a complete stop.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light when you need to slow down more quickly than drivers expect. This helps them notice you.
